gaps.sentence: The film was ___ good, but not brilliant.
gaps.hint: an adverb of degree is needed before 'good'
gaps.explanation: 'Quite' means fairly or rather; 'quiet' is an adjective meaning without noise.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: The ___ majority voted against the proposal.
gaps.explanation: 'An overwhelming majority' = far more than half.

gaps.sentence: I ___ seeing that man somewhere before.
The ___ issue of the magazine has an interview with the president.
gaps.explanation: 'Current' means happening or existing now; 'actual' means real as opposed to possible or estimated.

gaps.hint: the standard verb with television and sport
gaps.explanation: 'Watch television' is the fixed collocation; 'look' needs 'at', and 'see television' is not used.

gaps.sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
gaps.explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.
